name: Alt-right
summary: A loose, largely online white-nationalist and identitarian movement that emerged around 2008-2016, holding that white (European) identity is under attack from multiculturalism, egalitarianism and liberal elites. It favours racial separation or an ethnostate, sharply restricted immigration, nationalism and anti-globalism, and it rejects Enlightenment equality and the conservative establishment. Economics is a minor concern, with protectionist leanings.
scope: The mainstream white-nationalist 'Alternative Right' of 2010-2017 associated with Richard Spencer, Greg Johnson and Jared Taylor, with the Daily Stormer as its harder edge. It excludes the 'alt-lite' civic-nationalist wing and the paleoconservatism it grew from. Because the movement had no program, answers on economics and social issues are mostly low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Richard B. Spencer

keyFigures.name: Paul Gottfried
keyFigures.role: Paleoconservative whose 2008 talk on 'the Alternative Right' is dated as the movement's origin.

keyFigures.name: Greg Johnson
keyFigures.role: Editor of Counter-Currents, leading metapolitical theorist of North American white nationalism.

sources.usedFor: Spencer's views on gender roles, religion, democracy, abortion and health care.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Unlike mainstream US conservatives, members generally do not favour laissez-faire economics.

unions-good.rationale: No stated line; adherents are split between populist and market views.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not a focus; welfare is framed by race and citizenship rather than dependency.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Members invoke free speech to argue their views must be heard and see speech limits as authoritarian.

strong-leader.rationale: Anglin is reported to want authoritarian government, and Johnson is openly elitist; Trump was admired as a champion.

state-harmful.rationale: Spencer wants a state, an ethnostate, to secure a people; the movement is not anti-statist.

decide-locally.rationale: Some want to break the US into ethnic states, others want a strong white-majority nation; split.

traditional-family.rationale: Spencer wants women returned to childbearer and homemaker roles; the movement is anti-feminist.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Members show far less interest in homosexuality than US conservatives; some see it as immoral, others are tolerant.

abortion-legal.rationale: Spencer backs legal abortion on racial grounds while others oppose it; no common line.

more-religion-public.rationale: The movement is broadly secular, though some prize Christian heritage.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: It opposes multicultural and liberal efforts as an attack on white identity.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Anti-feminist and biologically essentialist about race and sex.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defends white or Western identity and heritage against perceived erasure.

gradual-change.rationale: Rejects the conservative establishment and Spencer calls for a new society, though it works through slow metapolitics.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Favours tighter restrictions on non-white immigration and some call for mass deportation.

nation-first.rationale: Openly nationalistic foreign policy and anti-globalism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Non-interventionist, opposes the war on terror and has no interest in spreading democracy.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No shared position; the Dark Enlightenment strand is techno-pessimist about democracy but not about technology.

revolution-justified.rationale: Rhetoric of radical rebirth and 'party like it's 1933', but the strategy is metapolitical; split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Johnson is elitist about who makes history but the movement is hostile to establishment experts.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Libertarian influence (Rothbard) exists but economics is not central.

one-party-rule.rationale: Authoritarian leanings but no party doctrine; split.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Neo-monarchists are reported among its adherents, and it rejects liberal democracy.

democracy-best.rationale: It rejects the liberal democratic basis of US governance, and Spencer questioned women's suffrage.

direct-votes.rationale: Spencer is not enthusiastic about voting; the movement is anti-egalitarian.

right-to-secede.rationale: Some envision breaking the US into ethnic states, others reject it.

natural-rulers.rationale: Anti-egalitarian: Johnson says history is made by elites, not the masses.

political-violence-never.rationale: Some celebrate violence; others disavow it as counterproductive.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Broadly secular; Spencer rejects Christianity as a universalist moral code.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Wants a state to protect a people; libertarian strand is minor.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Central: an ethnostate as a gathering point for Europeans.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Race, not class, is treated as the basis of identity and history.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Opposes efforts to correct historical injustices.

civilizational-union.rationale: Some promote a pan-white empire spanning Europe and North America.

restore-past-order.rationale: Frames white identity as under attack and rejects liberal modernity; but a new order is sought.

direct-action.rationale: Metapolitical culture-shifting strategy combined with street activism; split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Group identity, race, is the foundation; it rejects classical liberalism.

media-academia-power.rationale: Opposes political correctness and media, and uses 'Lügenpresse'-style attacks.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racial IQ hierarchies and 'race realism' are core.

national-rebirth.rationale: Sees white identity and Western civilization in decline and seeks metapolitical renewal.

territorial-expansion.rationale: A pan-white empire is floated by some but the mainstream is isolationist.

universal-morality.rationale: Rejects universalism and the Enlightenment; opposes Christianity for being universalist.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Opposes the close US-Israel tie and many are antisemitic, though Spencer admires Zionism as a model.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Envisions an ethnostate as a gathering point for all Europeans.

economic-freedom.rationale: Not laissez-faire; identity ranks above economics.

national-self-determination.rationale: A people's right to its own state is central to its ethnonationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Spencer has said women should return to childbearing and homemaking and not make foreign policy.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Favours exclusion or removal of non-whites rather than assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: Many believe in a plot to bring about 'white genocide' through replacement by non-whites.

national-mission.rationale: Has no interest in spreading democracy abroad.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Anti-establishment, opposes both conservative and liberal mainstream.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Johnson argues racial mixing causes hatred and conflict.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The statement concerns a socialist state, which the movement rejects; its wish for a strong ethnostate does not map onto it.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Its core claim is that diversity erodes cohesion, and Spencer and Johnson call for a white ethnostate.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Johnson and Spencer are openly elitist and reject egalitarian democracy, so lotteries among all citizens are rejected.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The movement demands sharply restricted immigration and a high bar to membership of the nation.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Anti-globalism and nationalism are core, and the movement rejects the EU-style union in favour of national sovereignty or ethnostates.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Adherents are split between Christians, pagans and secularists, so there is no common line on church governance.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Adherents are split between free-speech absolutists and those who want culture policed against 'degeneracy'; no common line.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: America-First nationalism and non-interventionism lead the movement to oppose entangling alliances and foreign wars.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: It attacks academia and liberal elites ('cultural Marxism') as disconnected, though Spencer is himself elitist.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Hierarchy of races and rejection of egalitarianism are central to the movement's quotations and scholarship.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Many leaders are atheist or pagan and reject Christianity, so creationism is not a movement demand.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Some figures decry 'degeneracy' while others are libertarian on speech; no common line.

central-bank-independence.rationale: No stated position; the movement is anti-establishment but has no common monetary line.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: No shared position; economics is de-emphasised and adherents differ on property rights versus communal duties.

character-from-environment.rationale: The movement rejects Enlightenment equality and holds that race and heredity shape people, as Spencer's statements show.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Spencer calls for a unified European homeland across current borders, grounded in shared ancestry.

ban-cartels.rationale: Economics is a minor concern for the movement.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Split: the movement rejects liberal democracy but opposes courts blocking nationalist policy.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Spencer holds traditional gender roles, and the movement opposes quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Its protectionist leanings favour national economic self-reliance.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Split: some embrace accelerationism, but Spencer and Johnson stress cultural and political metapolitics.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The movement centres European identity and heritage and attacks multicultural curricula.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The movement opposes affirmative action as anti-white discrimination.

public-money-creation.rationale: The movement has no program on money creation; some hold anti-bank views while others are market-oriented.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Economics is a minor concern and views range from decline narratives to market acceptance.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The movement advocates racial separation and opposes anti-discrimination law as an attack on white freedom of association.

elective-rulers.rationale: Spencer-style elitism favours rule by a European elite rather than mass democracy, though the movement has no monarchy program.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement is activist and aims at metapolitics and a political order for its people, so withdrawal is contrary to its aims.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The movement holds that white people should lead their own countries and rejects the idea that indigenous status should confer rule over settler descendants.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The movement's attitude to fascism is sympathetic or ambiguous and its adherents are strongly anti-communist, so they would not condemn both as equals.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The movement defends Confederate and similar monuments as part of European heritage, and attacks their removal.

paid-care-work.rationale: The movement favours traditional gender roles and does not support paying domestic labour as a policy.

office-by-exam.rationale: Adherents split: elitist rhetoric favours rule by the capable, but the movement has no civil-service program.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: No documented position; the movement is sceptical of liberal democracy but has no budget program.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The movement rejects egalitarianism and treats group disparities as natural rather than discriminatory.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Adherents split: some praise tradition over consumer culture, others the market; no common line.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The movement is documented as promoting the claim that Jews and other minorities conspire against white identity.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: No common economic line; Spencer backed state health care for white welfare while others favour markets.

religion-illusion.rationale: Views vary; Spencer and Johnson are critical of Christianity but treat religion and heritage as identity markers, not mere illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Economics is a minor concern with protectionist leanings, and the movement is split between admirers and critics of capitalism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The movement rejects egalitarianism and favours traditional gender roles, not economic transformation for equality.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The movement holds that European peoples have an ancestral right to their lands and an ethnostate, as Spencer and Johnson state.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Holocaust denial and minimisation circulate in the movement, and the Daily Stormer is openly denialist, though Spencer has equivocated.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The movement rejects egalitarian democracy and favours elite rule.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Spencer and the movement hold traditional gender roles and oppose transgender recognition.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Spencer and Johnson say left and right are both outdated and put identity first.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The movement holds that Islam and Muslim immigration threaten European identity.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The movement is mostly secular or pagan and does not ground authority in God; Spencer's elite rule is its own basis.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not an issue the movement addresses; adherents split.

social-market-economy.rationale: The movement leans protectionist and nationalist in economics and rejects laissez-faire, but is not a social-market movement.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Not a defining issue; the movement favours hierarchy and elites but has no stated position on dynastic rule.

property-franchise.rationale: The movement rejects equality but wants an ethnic, not property, qualification; the sources show no common line on property franchise.

reification.rationale: A Marxist idea; the movement is hostile to Marxism and treats race and identity, not class relations, as the basic social fact.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The movement attacks liberal media bias and elites but is not anti-wealth and holds no common line on press ownership.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The movement favours authority and an ethnostate; it prizes strong rulers but has no stated position on rule by standing law.

racial-franchise.rationale: The movement seeks a white ethnostate and restricted citizenship by race, which is its defining aim.

online-participation.rationale: The movement organised largely online but has no stated line on mass online political participation, and many adherents favour elite rule.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The movement is focused on race rather than religion and its adherents vary on religious questions, so the sources do not settle it.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The movement's targets are racial and ethnic, and its figures have criticised some boycotts, but its antisemitic fringe backs them, so adherents are split.

term-limits.rationale: The movement has no stated position on term limits and its adherents are split.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The movement wants an ethnostate and sharply restricted immigration, so non-citizen voting is rejected.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The movement rejects egalitarianism and holds biological, hierarchical views of sex and race.

culture-before-state.rationale: Greg Johnson's metapolitical strategy holds that cultural and ideological change must precede political power.

independent-unions.rationale: The movement has no labour programme and economics is a minor concern; adherents are split.

second-chamber.rationale: The movement has no program on legislative design, though it rejects mass democracy; adherents differ.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: No stated position; adherents are split between technocratic and traditionalist outlooks.

anonymous-payments.rationale: No stated position; the movement is split between wanting free-speech finance tools and favouring state power.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Spencer is secular-leaning while Johnson and others discuss religion and paganism; adherents split.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: No stated position; the movement favours an ethnostate but has no settled view on regional autonomy.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Spencer and Johnson explicitly state that whites have distinct racial interests and should organise for them, notably through an ethnostate.

racial-pride.rationale: Spencer's 'Hail our people' speech and the movement's identitarian stance make white pride central.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The alt-right opposed neoconservative interventionism and foreign wars, favouring nationalist restraint.

communal-electorates.rationale: The alt-right rejects multicultural group politics and wants one ethnically defined polity or ethnostate, not separate religious electorates.

sacred-nation.rationale: Its core theme is the white nation or people as a community with a shared destiny, as in Spencer's 'Hail our people' rhetoric.

shared-human-nature.rationale: It rejects Enlightenment egalitarianism and universal human equality in favour of innate racial difference.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Spencer and Johnson treat religion as secondary to race and some, like Spencer, reject Christianity as a universal creed; a shared universal truth runs against particularist identity.

farm-price-support.rationale: Economics is a minor concern with protectionist leanings, so farm support is plausible but never stated as a movement position.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The alt-right rejects egalitarian liberal democracy and favours an ethnically defined state, so competitive elections alone do not make a government legitimate to them.

race-social-construct.rationale: White-nationalist adherents hold that race is a biological reality and the basis of nations, as Spencer and Johnson state.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The movement's anti-feminism and rejection of egalitarianism make adherents opposed to state gender-equality bodies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The movement has no property doctrine and economics is a minor concern, so first-claim ownership is not a shared position.

national-church-status.rationale: Adherents are split between Christian traditionalists and pagan or secular members, and the movement has no line on church status.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The movement's identitarian thought links a people to its ancestral land, though blood and descent matter more than soil.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Economics is a minor concern and adherents differ.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Economics is a minor concern; welfare for whites only is a recurrent but split view.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Spencer's 'Hail Trump' speech celebrates a leader embodying the people against establishments.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The movement rejects egalitarianism and multiculturalism as the real harm and holds that white identity is the one under attack.

multipolar-world.rationale: Spencer and others favoured separate civilizational or ethnic blocs, and the movement was anti-globalist.

material-over-identity.rationale: Racial and cultural identity is the movement's core concern, ahead of economics.

notes: The movement had no formal program and splintered after Charlottesville (2017). Strands differ on Jews, Christianity, and an ethnostate versus a white-majority nation. Only one primary source (speech excerpts) could be opened; most of the primary writings were inaccessible.
